switch.name: Switch
switch.purpose: Use Switch for an immediate on/off setting where the changed state persists and the label explains the active outcome.
switch.referenceRationale: The ZIP reference defines the visual benchmark: 48 by 28 track, expanding thumb on press, clear on/off color, and spring feedback. Design System owns color, type, density, state, motion, and accessibility semantics.

anatomy.rule: Names the setting as the active outcome.
Shows off, on, focus, error, and disabled status without changing size.
Moves and stretches during press to communicate direct manipulation.
Explains consequence or policy only when the label is not enough.

variants.description: High-impact setting that needs human review before use.

switch.statePrecedence: disabled > error > pressed > focus > on > off

Energy.decision: Use Energy for on/off track, disabled, and error color.
Energy.behavior: Energy makes state visible before reading the label.
Energy.example: Driver alerts use accent when on and neutral when off.
Energy.test: Verify contrast for on, off, error, and disabled.
Energy.rejectIf: State depends only on thumb position or raw color.

Voice.decision: Use Voice for labels and support text.
Voice.example: Use 'Send driver alerts' instead of vague on/off copy.
Voice.rejectIf: The label is hidden or ambiguous.

Frame.decision: Use Frame for track, thumb, radius, row spacing, and density.
Frame.behavior: Frame keeps the control stable across states.
Frame.example: Settings rows align in mobile and desktop lists.
Frame.test: Verify no track or thumb clipping across densities.

Depth.decision: Use Depth only for thumb separation.
Depth.behavior: Depth separates thumb from track without decorative elevation.
Depth.example: Thumb shadow stays subtle on both on and off states.
Depth.test: Verify shadow does not replace state.
Depth.rejectIf: Depth is used as the only state signal.

Momentum.decision: Use Momentum touch for thumb movement and press stretch.
Momentum.example: Thumb moves with spring and stretches while pressed.
Momentum.test: Verify touch motion and reduced-motion behavior.
Momentum.rejectIf: Motion uses raw duration or curve.

State.decision: Use State for disabled, error, pressed, focus, on, and off precedence.
State.example: Disabled blocks toggling even when on.
State.rejectIf: State is visual only or contradictory.

Tone.decision: Use Tone for direct operational labels.
Tone.rejectIf: Copy hides risk or policy meaning.

Growth.decision: Use Growth for reusable persistent settings across products.
Growth.behavior: Growth keeps API stable across settings surfaces.
Growth.example: The same switch works in driver app and fleet console.
Growth.test: Verify the contract supports settings lists and cards.
Growth.rejectIf: A product forks one-off switch behavior.

Symbol.decision: Use Symbol only when an adjacent icon clarifies the setting.
Symbol.behavior: Symbol does not replace label or state.
Symbol.example: A notification icon can support alert settings.
Symbol.test: Verify icons have text labels nearby.

Iconography.decision: Use Iconography for optional leading affordances outside the track.
Iconography.behavior: Iconography supports context without entering the track.
Iconography.example: Bell icon appears before alert setting label.
Iconography.test: Verify no decorative icon replaces state.

Accessibility.decision: Use Accessibility for role switch, visible label, keyboard toggle, focus, and state announcement.
Accessibility.behavior: Accessibility exposes on/off state to assistive tech.
Accessibility.example: Switch announces checked state and toggles with Space.
Accessibility.test: Verify role, label, aria-checked, focus, disabled, and error association.
Accessibility.rejectIf: It is implemented as visual-only checkbox without switch semantics.

productExamples.example: Turn route and balance alerts on or off.
Enable wallet policy settings that persist after save.

do: Keep the active outcome in the label.
Show immediate feedback when value changes.
dont: Do not use for multi-select choices.
Do not require Save if the setting is not immediate.
Do not use when the user must choose one option from many.
info: Use Checkbox when the action is selection or consent; use Switch when the product state turns on or off.

contextDensityStrategy.layout: full-width settings rows with clear touch space
readable configuration rows and remote-focus surfaces

tests: Renders visible label and role switch.
agentInstructions: Use Switch only for persistent on/off settings.
Ask before using Switch for money, permissions, compliance, or automatic approvals.
Use Checkbox for selection and Radio/Select for choice sets.
rejectIf: The value does not persist or has no immediate effect.
It replaces Checkbox in multi-select lists.
Motion or color bypasses Design System tokens.
